title: Bilal ibn Rabah
hook: freed from slavery, the caller to prayer, whose footsteps were heard in the garden (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday: ahl al-bayt, the people of the house, blessed in the prayer. Your line was and on his family.

It's the dawn prayer in Medina, still half dark. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, turns to one man with a question. Bilal, tell me the deed you hope in most, because I heard the sound of your footsteps ahead of me in paradise. This man has come up before. He lay under a rock on the hot sand and said one word: one. He was bought and set free. His voice called the prayer. And now he's asked: what are you doing that no one sees? Today begins a new part, the early believers, and Bilal opens it.
screen: `THE DAWN PRAYER, HALF DARK.` → `WHAT DEED DO YOU HOPE IN MOST?` → `YOUR FOOTSTEPS, AHEAD OF ME.`

segments.voice: Start with today's word. A muezzin, in Arabic mu'adhdhin, is the one who gives the adhan, the call to prayer. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn Umar tells how the call began in Medina: the companions talked over how to gather people for prayer, and the Prophet said: Bilal, get up and call to the prayer. So the voice that once said only one, under the rock, became the voice the whole town woke to. That's the public Bilal. The footsteps are about the private one. The report is in Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah. The Prophet asks, Bilal thinks, and he doesn't name the adhan at all. He says: I have done nothing I hope in more than this. Whenever I purify myself, by night or by day, I pray with that purification whatever prayer was written for me. That's it. Wudu, the washing before prayer, then a short prayer nobody asked for. A version in the collection of al-Tirmidhi names it as two units. Not a fast, not a famous act. A habit done in an empty room, so small no one would think to ask about it. And it was heard in the garden. Muslims may pray a voluntary prayer known as the two units after wudu, and this hadith is behind it. A man with a very public job pointed to a private thing he did. The voice is what people remembered. The footsteps are what was heard ahead.
screen: `MUEZZIN: THE ONE WHO CALLS.` · `BILAL, GET UP AND CALL.` · `THE DEED: A PRAYER AFTER WUDU.` · `SMALL, PRIVATE, HEARD AHEAD.` · then, large: `THE FOOTSTEPS OF BILAL.`

segments.voice: If you pray, you can do what Bilal did: make wudu, then pray two short units, with nobody asking and nobody watching. If you don't, wash your hands and face slowly with cool water, then give the next minute to stillness, for no reason anyone else would know.
Muezzin. In Arabic, mu'adhdhin: the one who calls the adhan, as Bilal did in Medina. Today's word.
Your line: the footsteps of bilal. The quiet deed was the one he named. That's day eight hundred twenty-three.

howItsDone: In mosques a muezzin gives the adhan before each prayer, and Muslims may pray two short voluntary units after making wudu, often called the sunnah of wudu, following this hadith about Bilal.

chat.says: What deed did Bilal say he hoped in most?
options: A short prayer after every wudu, by night or day, that nobody asked him for.
Giving the call to prayer in Medina, the job everyone knew him for.
Holding firm under the rock in Mecca while he was being tortured.
chat.meaning: In Bukhari, Bilal didn't name the adhan: whenever he purified himself, he prayed whatever prayer was written for him.

Bilal.meaning: a freed companion whose voice called the prayer

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 604 (Ibn Umar: Bilal, get up and call to the prayer)
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3689 (Bilal: two units after wudu)

notes: Bukhari 1149, 604 and Tirmidhi 3689 numbering and paraphrases: confirm; Bukhari's wording is 'what was written for me', and the 'two units' detail is from Tirmidhi's version.
Index hook says 'the first caller to prayer'; 'first' dropped under the claims rule (Bukhari 604 shows him told to call, not that he was first).
'muezzin comes from mu'adhdhin' in the original note: confirm.
Earlier Bilal days (hot sand, freed by Abu Bakr, the roof, the first adhan) are only recalled in one line; this day leads with the footsteps hadith.
Editor: removed 'in front of everyone' (Bukhari 1149 places the question at the dawn prayer, nothing more); 'Muslims pray' softened to 'may pray'; fixed garbled practice line about wudu.
